submission.natural_language_explanation: The negative pole fires on the tokens that state a specific amount of a measurable property - a numeral or number word together with the unit or measured noun it quantifies (2 kilometres, 300 kilograms, 40 metres deep, 8 hours, 12 tonnes, 20 degrees, 500 litres, forty-five minutes) - peaking on or just after the numeral and its unit noun and staying up across the rest of the measure phrase. Activation drops sharply, typically to under half, when the same property is described qualitatively or evaluated with no amount (very heavy, quite warm, a long way, deep and cold, exhausting, a lot, many), while swapping one amount for another (20 degrees vs 30 degrees, 10 vs 12 kilometres) leaves it essentially unchanged.
